name: Accounts

Deliberately kept minimal (email + password hash, one Register command) — the same generic-subdomain restraint the notes package documents for itself: this presupposes nothing about roles, permissions, or what an account is FOR beyond being able to authenticate. source_text:
# web.rs's accounts_register_route/accounts_login_route/accounts_me_route
# tests dispatch into this -- embryonaut_bluebooks' own accounts package
# (vendor/embryonaut_bluebooks/accounts/bluebook/accounts.bluebook,
# lifeadelics repo), minus its own "Listing" query (see below). Its OWN
# fixture directory, not folded into checkout_fixture alongside it --
# confirmed live: adding a second top-level Hecks.hecksagon/bluebook
# chapter named "Accounts" there flipped bin/project_wasm's own
# primary-domain selection away from "CheckoutFixture" (alphabetically,
# "Accounts" sorts first), silently dropping Event/Registration from
# checkout_fixture.ir.json's own aggregate list and breaking every api.rs
# presentation test that reads it. A dedicated, single-chapter fixture
# has no such ambiguity.
Hecks.bluebook "Accounts" do
  vision "A small, reusable admin-identity capability: one login record per human, so a consuming project's own admin UI never has to hand-roll password storage. Deliberately kept minimal (email + password hash, one Register command) — the same generic-subdomain restraint the notes package documents for itself: this presupposes nothing about roles, permissions, or what an account is FOR beyond being able to authenticate. A consuming project that syncs this into another system (e.g. a headless CMS's own users collection, for single-sign-on) does that syncing itself, in its own driving adapter — this package has no concept of any other system existing."
  supporting

  aggregate "Account" do
    description "One admin's login identity — email plus an already-hashed password. Hashing/verifying happens in a consuming project's own driving adapter (this package has no opinion on bcrypt vs. anything else); the domain only ever stores and returns the hash."

    identified_by :email

    attribute :email,         AccountEmail
    attribute :password_hash, PasswordHash

    value_object "AccountEmail" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an account has an email") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "PasswordHash" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a password hash is never blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Register" do
      goal "Create a new admin account with an already-hashed password"

      attribute :email,         AccountEmail
      attribute :password_hash, PasswordHash

      sets :email
      sets :password_hash

      emits "AccountRegistered"
    end

    # THE REAL PACKAGE'S OWN "Listing" QUERY IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT --
    # none of web.rs's accounts_register_route/accounts_login_route/
    # accounts_me_route dispatch or need it (login reads raw instances
    # via dispatch::read + instances_for, not a declared query), and its
    # own `order_by "email.value"` exposed a real, previously-undiscovered
    # Ruby/Rust parser gap: Ruby's builder accepts a STRING order_by
    # argument naming a nested value-object member; hecks-parse (Rust)
    # refuses it outright ("reads as text (expected one of: symbol)") --
    # confirmed live, this exact fixture is the first time that package's
    # own real source ever ran through Rust's parser-parity corpus at
    # all (it normally only loads via uses_embryonaut_bluebook, from
    # lifeadelics, a separate repo this corpus never parses). A real,
    # separate parser bug worth a follow-up, not something this fixture
    # needs to work around by testing a query nothing here exercises.
  end
end
